claims.statement: Amycretin is a single investigational molecule containing two covalently linked peptide analogs that act as a GLP-1 receptor agonist and an amylin receptor agonist, intended to combine appetite-regulating and metabolic effects in one unimolecular co-agonist.

context.formulation: subcutaneous and oral formulations in development

claims.statement: Amycretin has no regulatory approval anywhere and remains an investigational compound in active clinical development by Novo Nordisk (phase 1b/2a completed for subcutaneous obesity use, phase 2 completed for type 2 diabetes, phase 3 development announced); no amycretin drug product is legally marketed for human use.

claims.statement: In a phase 1b/2a randomised, placebo-controlled trial in adults with obesity/overweight (n=125; 101 amycretin, 24 placebo), subcutaneous amycretin produced dose-dependent weight reductions from baseline reaching 24.3% at the 60 mg maintenance dose by week 36, versus minimal change (-1.1% to +2.3%) with placebo; no weight-loss plateau was reported at the higher doses studied.

context.population: adults 18-55 years, BMI 27.0-39.9 kg/m^2, no major illnesses (n=125)
context.formulation: investigational subcutaneous amycretin, multiple dose arms
context.doseText: trial protocol dose arms of 1.25 mg, 5 mg, 20 mg, and 60 mg maintenance doses over 20-36 weeks; not a use recommendation

extractedEvidence.pageOrSection: 60 mg maintenance dose, week 36 weight reduction from baseline

claims.statement: In a phase 2, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-finding trial (NCT06542874) in 448 adults with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%) on stable metformin, amycretin reduced body weight up to 14.5% (subcutaneous) and 10.1% (oral) from baseline at week 36 versus approximately 2.5-2.6% with placebo, and reduced HbA1c up to 1.8 percentage points (subcutaneous) and 1.5 percentage points (oral) versus 0.2-0.4 points with placebo.

context.population: adults with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 7.0-10.0% on stable metformin (n=448)
context.formulation: investigational subcutaneous (0.4-40 mg once weekly) and oral (6-50 mg once daily) amycretin
context.doseText: trial protocol dose arms; subcutaneous 0.4 mg-40 mg once weekly, oral 6 mg-50 mg once daily over 36 weeks; not a use recommendation

claims.statement: Across early-phase trials, amycretin was associated with a high rate of gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; mostly mild to moderate), dose-dependent injection-site dysaesthesia, a transient heart-rate increase of about 10 beats per minute, antidrug antibody formation in 21-29% of participants, and at least one reported case of mild gallstone pancreatitis in the phase 1b/2a obesity trial.

context.population: adults with obesity/overweight enrolled in the phase 1b/2a subcutaneous trial

claims.statement: Amycretin is not an approved drug and no human amycretin product is legally sold, yet research-chemical vendors sell it labeled 'for research use only, cannot be used for human consumption' while consumer-facing peptide content sites publish trial weight-loss figures alongside purchase-oriented quizzes and affiliate links to compounded weight-loss alternatives; unsupervised acquisition and self-administration of vendor-sourced amycretin is not supported by any human safety or efficacy evidence and falls outside the population, dosing, and monitoring conditions studied in the clinical trials.
